title: Indivisible Yolo’s No Kings Vote Early Events

description:
Indivisible Yolo will host three No Kings Vote Early events across Davis, West Sacramento and Woodland on Oct. 17. The mass participation events will build upon the energy of previous mass protests as the group works to turn protest power into early voter action. Local residents are invited to attend one or more of the three community events and bring their ballots to submit. Hosted information booths will provide voter assistance, including voter registration, details on when and where to vote, as well as information on California ballot initiatives and efforts to combat voter suppression. 
The Woodland No Kings Vote Early event will take place from 10am-1pm at the Old Courthouse, 725 Court Street. The West Sacramento event will take place from 10am-2pm at Trinity Presbyterian Church, 1500 Park Boulevard. The Davis event will take place from 2-4pm at G Street Plaza, 301 G Street. To sign up for one or more events, visit https://www.indivisibleyolo.org/no-kings-vote-early. 
Indivisible Yolo is the local chapter of the nationwide grassroots movement Indivisible. Indivisible Yolo’s mission is to promote progressive policies by activating people to engage in their democracy at all levels of government. The group organizes and advocates for policy goals and to get out the vote to elect candidates who pursue those policies. These complementary efforts ensure democracy works for everyone and that those in power do, too. For more information: www.indivisibleyolo.org.

title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge
location: Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis, 254 Old Davis Road, Davis, California, 95616
description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. 
Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. 
While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.

title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection
location: Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis, 254 Old Davis Road, Davis, California, 95616
description: This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.

title: Birds & Bikes
location: Axis Gallery, 625 S St, Sacramento, 95811, United States
description:
Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. 
The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. 
Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop-Up Shop. 
Participating artists include Antonia Price, Sokthea Chan*, Linda Clark Johnson, Nathan Coldwater, Kate Farrall, Sandy Fong Whetstone, Cara Gregor*, Jordin Hinton, Heather Hogan*, Maris Kaplan, Tanya Lieberman, Elise Mahan*, Lo’Vonia Parks, Judy Coates Perez, Samuel Rose, Jenna Savage, Michelle Sharf, and Alex Williams. title: Why We Ride: Author talk with Peter Flax
location: Shields Library, 167
description:
Join us for an inspiring and enlightening look at the reasons that make people fall in love with bicycle riding! Author Peter Flax will share his insights into the creation and production of Live to Ride: Finding Joy and Meaning on a Bicycle, his 2024 book which explores the unifying dynamics of bicycle culture.
 

The book argues that everyone who rides—whether they commute, enjoy nature, or race—has more in common than they might realize. Part of the discussion will focus on a section contextualizing the significance of groundbreaking bike lanes constructed decades ago in Davis—and how Flax was aided by photography and documents from our Archives and Special Collections Department.
 

This talk is free and open to all. Please register in advance to reserve your spot.

About the Speaker
Peter Flax is a Los Angeles-based writer and editor who frequently writes about cycling. He is the former editor in chief of Bicycling magazine and was editorial director at Red Bull Media house. His work has been published by dozens of magazines, including Outside, Time, Alta Journal, Men’s Health, and Runner’s World. Live to Ride was his first book. Flax has lived in Los Angeles for 13 years without a car, doing roughly 100,000 miles of bike commuting in that timeframe.

title: Imagining America National Gathering
description:
Join over 500 participants from the IA network and the University of California, Davis and Yolo Bioregion community (a geographic and cultural area that includes the cities of Davis, Woodland, Winters, West Sacramento, and surrounding areas) to engage in deep learning, collaboration, and transformative creativity on the theme of Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times. We will activate spaces across the UC Davis campus, in the City of Davis, and at community-hosted site visits. 
Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times calls us to re-story and honor the places, knowledges, relationships, and ecologies that have been made broken through centuries of violence and abandonment, and the current intensifying fear and repression. We know that our communities are tired, and we know that being together revives our collective spirit, giving us the strength and inspiration we need in troubled times. In this moment of upheaval, the 2026 IA National Gathering draws participants to Davis, CA in the spirit of mending the roots of our connections, and to “awaken,” as Buddhist monk and activist Thích Nhất Hạnh teaches, “from the illusion of our separateness.”

Representatives of local agencies championing each challenge track will serve as subject matter experts; students will also have access to mentors.

 

Who: 

The event is hosted by DataLab and the UC Davis Library, and is open to students of all backgrounds and experience levels, from any university or college. No prior hackathon experience is required—just curiosity and an eagerness to build something that matters. Participants are strongly encouraged to form interdisciplinary teams and include peers from a variety of majors. Each team may have a maximum of five people and has to include at least one UC Davis student.

 

Why:

Contribute to solving a problem in your community

Get experience working on a cross-functional team

Release an open-source productThe winners are invited to UN Open Source Week at United Nations Headquarters in New York! Travel expenses will be covered for the winning team. 

Schedule:

Kickoff Day (October 23)Wrap-up and Judging (October 24) Participation is required for at least part of both days.

 

Learn More:

At UC Santa Cruz's hackathon in November 2025, the winning team, FireForm, built an AI-powered voice-to-text tool that lets firefighters complete required documentation by speaking naturally instead of typing. They continued developing it after the event, and it has since been certified as a United Nations Digital Public Good. 

 

At UC San Diego (May 2026), the winning team created FireLink, an SMS-based platform that delivers wildfire updates to residents with no internet or smartphone required.

 

This Open Access Week event underlines the UC Davis Library’s commitment to open science.

title: Author Talk: Market Memories Cookbook with Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan (Davis)
location: Blanchard Room, Mary L Stephens Davis Branch Library
description:
The cookbook, which has 92 recipes, arranged by season, also tells the story of how the county’s iconic market evolved as the brainchild of four young Davis people, including co-author Ann M. Evans, with a few farmers selling fruits and vegetables from the back of their pick-ups, to one of the most recognized farmers market in the United States. 

The story is told through personal essays by the co-founders and others with seminal involvement, 32 anecdotal quotes from vendors, shoppers, and elected officials, and a timeline chronicling market highlights over 50 years, as well as an in- memoriam page, commemorating the market vendors who are deceased.

The book is illustrated by Ann and Georgeanne as well, with beautiful pen and ink and watercolor washes for fruit and vegetables and flowers in all the seasons.

location: Robert Mondavi Institute - Sensory Building, Sensory Theater
description:
Join us for this quarter's Savor event: Fresh Starts: How California Farmers Markets Changed the Way We Eat.
 

The formation of the Davis Farmers Market 50 years ago was a revolutionary movement to connect consumers directly to farmers and helped shape the fresh flavors of California cuisine. Markets have been a cornerstone of the community and have also played a pivotal role in food access, especially during supply chain shortages and widespread food recalls. Inevitably, markets have evolved. Join us as we explore the history, impact and changing role of farmers markets in local communities. 

The event will feature a panel of leading industry experts including:
 

Ann Evans, UC Davis alumna, co-founder of the Davis Farmers Market and Davis Food Co-op, author and former mayor and city council member of the City of DavisSam Greenlee, chief executive officer of Alchemist Community Development CorporationChutharat Sae Tong, co-owner of Majka Pizzeria and Bakery in SacramentoModerator Catherine Brinkley, associate professor in Human Ecology, Community and Regional Development at UC Davis 

A pop-up exhibit from the library's Archives and Special Collections will be on display.

 

The event includes a welcome reception, a hosted bar and appetizers. Tickets are $25/person ($15/students). 

 

The Savor lecture series is a collaboration between the Robert Mondavi Institute for Wine and Food Science and the UC Davis Library.

At a time when many of us are feeling anxious or disconnected, creating spaces for joy, belonging, and connection feels more important than ever. For one day, I-House is your house. Come be part of it.

Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.

title: 2nd Friday ArtAbout – Monthly Downtown Davis Art Walk (Free!)
description:
Join Davis’s beloved 2nd Friday ArtAbout – a free monthly self-guided artwalk coordinated by the Pence Gallery! Every second Friday, stroll downtown Davis to discover fresh exhibits, opening receptions, live music, hands-on activities, and direct chats with local and regional artists at 10+ galleries, co-ops, and businesses. 
Support our vibrant arts scene, uncover unique talent and styles, and soak up the lively energy – ideal for friends, families, dates, or solo adventures. Many venues offer complimentary refreshments like wine and snacks. 
Free – no tickets required! 

Runs approximately 5:00–9:00 PM (venue receptions vary—check the monthly guide for specifics).
Grab the printed guide (with map & details) the week of at the Pence Gallery or participating spots, or download it at pencegallery.org/events/artabout/.

Interested in hosting as a venue, artist, or business? Visit https://pencegallery.org/events/artabout/ to fill out the corresponding forms. Please submit events 3 weeks in advance via the form on the site to be included in the guide and promotions. 
Stay in the loop: facebook.com/davisartabout 
Come celebrate local creativity downtown – see you on the next second Friday! 🎨✨

title: DJUSD Board Meetings
location: City Hall Community Chambers, 23 Russell Blvd, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
DJUSD Board meetings offer insight on how the school district remains responsive to the community’s values, beliefs, and priorities. The Board meetings occur on every first and third Thursday, in the City of Davis Community Chambers. 23 Russell Boulevard. Public session starts at 6:30 PM.  Meetings are cablecast live on Channel 17 (Comcast) or streamed on the DJUSD-TV website. 
  
The Davis Joint Unified School District’s Board of Education is comprised of five community members, responsible for setting district policy, approving the budget, and hiring the superintendent for schools in Davis, California. The agendas for the meetings are posted at least 72 hours in advance. 
  
For more information on special meetings, agendas, public comment, and more, visit the DJUSD Board site.

title: Human Relations Commission Meetings
location: City Hall Community Chambers, 23 Russell Blvd, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July). 
  
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site. 
  
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council. 
  
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
